title: Describe one Match with records
why: A Match needs clear records before it can change state. You define who plays and which Round is current.
outcome: Build 1v1 Match and Round records with explicit IDs and reject bad membership.

steps.title: Name the parts of a Match
steps.question: What does a Match record own?
explanation: A Match is one timed competition between two sides. In 1v1 each side is one player. In 2v2 each side is a team of two players.
A Round is one Problem inside the Match. The reference Match has three Rounds. Each Round has its own code and visible tests. Only the Match score carries over.

You will make small practice records first. They mirror the reference records in packages/arena-model/src/model.ts and packages/arena-game/src/records.ts, but they use your own local names. The team destination will map these ideas later.

vocabulary.meaning: One timed competition between two sides.
One player in 1v1, or one two-player team in 2v2.

steps.title: See Match, Round, sides, players
steps.question: Which field holds the current Round?

vocabulary.meaning: Gameplay state of one side: coding, running, submitted, evaluating, locked in. Presence (online/offline) never replaces it.

steps.title: Explicit IDs prevent confusion
steps.question: Why reject a duplicate player?
explanation: In C you might use an array index and trust the caller. Here each player has a string userId and each side has a sideId. The Match authority later uses these IDs to decide membership.

Reference preview: packages/arena-game/src/records.ts defines Participant { userId, sideId } and MatchRecord with participants. Reference preview: packages/arena-game/src/match-authority.ts defines requireMember and sideOf, which throw NotMemberError for outsiders. You only read these files now. You build the small practice version next.
Like strcmp in C, identity checks compare exact strings. A wrong ID is a membership problem, not a type problem.

vocabulary.meaning: The module that checks membership, orders Match commands, and stamps revisions. It does not run Judge work or network code.

title: Allow only legal phase changes
why: Match phase decides what players may do. An illegal change must keep old state and explain itself.
outcome: Implement round and side transitions with useful errors.

steps.title: Why phases gate actions
steps.question: Which phase allows Run and Submit?
explanation: Match phase is the authoritative Match state. Only CODING permits Run and Submit. The server also rejects both at the exact Match deadline.

Reference Match phase order: ROUND_INTRO, CODING, then SUBMITTED, EVALUATING, SCORE_REVEAL, then next Round or Match end. Your practice model uses the reference phase names from packages/arena-model/src/model.ts: MATCH_FOUND, ROUND_INTRO, CODING, SCORE_REVEAL, ROUND_COMPLETE, MATCH_COMPLETE.
You need this now because later lessons gate Run, Submit, and Reveal on the phase.

vocabulary.meaning: The authoritative Match state. Only CODING permits Run and Submit.

hints: Answer: CODING.
Find the phase list.

steps.title: See legal and illegal arrows
steps.question: What happens on an illegal arrow?
explanation: ROUND_INTRO can go to CODING. CODING has no generic exit in the reference table; only a special reveal helper leaves it. SCORE_REVEAL can go to ROUND_INTRO, ROUND_COMPLETE, or MATCH_COMPLETE. An illegal request keeps the old phase and returns an error.
hints: Point at ROUND_INTRO to CODING.
Point at the empty CODING exits.
Compare with a switch statement that rejects default.

steps.title: Round phase versus side activity
steps.question: Why do sides move independently?
explanation: The Round phase is global. Player status is per side: coding, running, submitted, evaluating, locked in. One side evaluating never freezes the other side.

Reference preview: packages/arena-model/src/transitions.ts defines canTransition, canRun, canSubmit, canSideTransition, canSideRun, canSideSubmit, and publishRoundReveal. CODING to SCORE_REVEAL is absent from the generic table on purpose. You read it now and build a small practice copy next.
In C terms, think of one global enum plus one enum per side. Presence (online/offline) is separate and never an activity change.

vocabulary.meaning: Per-round score disclosure after evaluation. Hidden details appear only here.

title: Let only members act
why: The Match authority is the final check for game commands. Outsiders must fail before state changes.
outcome: Resolve a trusted actor to a side and reject outsiders.

steps.title: Membership comes before action
steps.question: What runs before any Match command?
explanation: Membership resolution. The caller proves who they are. The Match authority finds their side. Only then does the command run.
This matters now because Run and Submit later need the same gate. A wrong ID is a membership issue, not a missing type assertion.

vocabulary.meaning: An explicit solution sent for hidden evaluation. Allowed only during CODING.

title: Decide by injected time
why: The Match has one server clock. Tests must supply time instead of sleeping.
outcome: Accept before the deadline, reject at equality, and replace the old countdown.

steps.title: One Match deadline
steps.question: When does the Match stop accepting actions?
explanation: At the Match deadline. The Match deadline is the end of the one Match-wide server clock. A Submission accepted before the deadline may still count if judging finishes inside a short grace period.
You need this now because Run and Submit both check now against deadline. Equality is already closed.

vocabulary.meaning: The end of the one Match-wide server clock. New Run and Submit stop exactly there.

hints: Answer: exactly at the deadline.

steps.title: See Clock as a boundary
steps.question: Why pass now as a parameter?
explanation: A Clock boundary is an object with now(). Tests supply a fixed now, so they run fast and stay exact. Production supplies real time later. This is dependency injection: pass the dependency into the function instead of reading global time inside it.

vocabulary.meaning: Practice boundary { now(): number }. Tests inject fixed time.

steps.title: Strict less-than, not inclusive
steps.question: Why is equality closed here but open in the old rule?
explanation: The old teaching rule isSubmitWindowOpen used secondsLeft > 0, where 0 was false. The Match rule isBeforeDeadline(now, deadline) uses now < deadline, where equality is false. Same shape, new context: server time versus one deadline.
In C, 99 < 100 is true and 100 < 100 is false. TypeScript behaves the same for numbers. The limit of the C comparison: TypeScript number is not a C int, but the ordering logic matches.
You will explicitly replace the simplified seconds-left model in src/rules.ts. Keep membership and phase checks separate.
